Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The successful candidate must be flexible to cover additional hours as required by the needs of the surgery and be happy to work between 7:45 and 18:30 on a rota basis. The core responsibilities of the receptionist are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record

title: Ward Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised, motivated and approachable individual with previous medical administration experience. The role is a working on site only and you are required to live within 1 hour distance of all three of our hospital sites at Ashford, Canterbury and Margate and our Head Office in Betteshanger, Deal, Kent. Any applicant outside of this area will automatically be declined. You will be expected to travel to our Margate site for initial training and to all of our hospital sites as needed and directed. If you are looking for an exciting opportunity to develop your career within a busy medical environment and believe you have the skills and experience, we are looking for, we would love to hear from you. As a Ward Administrator, you will play a key role in supporting the Ward at our Ashford and Canterbury sites as part of a 7 day working rota which will include regular weekend working. Your responsibilities will include: Ensure that patients are admitted and discharged on the relevant in-house systems and that copy EDNs are filed in the patient notes on discharge. Organise, scan and attach Ward and Theatre documentation. Liaise with clinical, finance, admin colleagues, Consultants and colleagues from EKHUFT to ensure the smooth running of the hospitals. Ensure that admission packs and notes are prepared and available prior to patient admission. Liaising professionally with patients and Consultants. Using in house software to maintain accurate patient records, waiting lists and clinic management information. Managing multiple priorities and conflicting demands in a busy environment. We are looking for someone who is: Highly organised and able to work accurately under pressure. Able to work across sites as and when required and dictated by the line manager. Friendly, professional and approachable. An excellent communicator, both verbally and in writing. Confident in managing competing priorities and working to strict deadlines. Experienced in a medical administration environment. Comfortable working independently while also being a strong team player Job Purpose To provide clerical and administrative support to the hospital management and clinical staff at the Ashford and Canterbury sites. Key Relationships Clinical Director Head of Clinical Services Ward Manager Ward nurses Outpatient nurses Reception Team Bookings Team Finance Team Patients Consultants Key Responsibilities Provide administrative assistance to the Clinical Director, clinical management, and nursing teams. Ensure that patient treatment, day case and inpatient stay information is recorded on the systems accurately, completely and in a timely manner. Organise, scan and attach documentation to patient records. Ensure that patients are admitted and discharged on the relevant systems and that copy EDNs are filed in the patient notes on discharge. Liaise with clinical, finance and admin colleagues as well as consultants and colleagues from EKHUFT to ensure the smooth running of the hospitals. Plan and organise the transfer of patient notes and provision of relevant documentation, using the NHS PAS / Allscripts and inhouse systems, ensuring their availability for the nursing team, consultants prior to patient admission and for the coders after patient discharge. Assist in the preparation reports, both ad hoc and regularly scheduled, internal and external, ensuring accuracy and timeliness of submission. Provide excellent customer care, showing tact, empathy and discretion in dealing with patients and relatives. Answer and direct phone calls and emails, providing excellent customer service and liaising with colleagues across the business to ensure that queries are dealt with efficiently. Assist with bed planning. Assist with the annual review of departmental policies and procedures to ensure they reflect good practice and ensure requirements are complied with. Assist in the annual review and updating of hospital SLAs. Order ward and office supplies Assist in the ordering of theatre equipment when required. Financial Liaise effectively with the finance and administration teams to handle and resolve patient queries. Liaise with the Finance and coding team to ensure that patient stays can be coded and invoiced in a timely manner. Business Development Develop in depth service knowledge and offer information about our services to our clients. Keep up to date with new services offered. Arrange meetings with any new prospective clinical colleagues. Promote, be available and offer tours of the unit to any patients wishing to view the ward prior to choosing Spencer. Quality Assist the clinical management in retaining the ISO9001:2015 (Quality Management), ISO14001:2015 (Environmental) and Investors in People accreditations. Maintain an accurate medical record system. Ensure all computer systems are kept up to date at all times e.g., EDN, Sunrise, NJR, Patient Centre and Compucare Assist in any clerical duties considered necessary for the smooth running of the hospital, such as helping to locate consultants, collate and file all patients notes on admission and / or discharge, ensuring that they are complete and in the correct order, Assist with any stock take requests. Assist with audits and site inspections as directed by the Clinical Director Carry out any other administrative duty that facilitates the smooth running of the ward reception as directed by any clinical colleague. Workforce Participate in in-house training sessions, attend meetings and discussions as and when required. Maintain stock levels of all pre-assessment paperwork, forms and pathways. Work as part of a team providing cover at all sites as and when required. Prepare and maintain off-duty rotas for the ward, making optimum use of staff over a six week period. Equal Opportunities It is the aim of the hospital to ensure that no job applicant or employee receives less favourable treatment on the grounds of age, sex, race, colour, nationality or ethnic or national origins, or is not placed at a disadvantage by conditions or requirements which cannot be shown to be justifiable. To this end, the hospital has an Equal Opportunities Policy, and it is for each employee to contribute to its success. Health & Safety All Employees must be aware of the responsibility placed on them under the Health and Safety at Work Act (1974), to ensure that the agreed safety procedures are carried out to maintain a safe environment for employees and visitors. Individual employees should also refer to specific health and safety requirements within their own job descriptions. Data Protection If required to do so, to obtain, process and/or use information held on a computer or word-processor in a fair and lawful way. To hold data only for the specific registered purpose, and not to use or disclose it in any way incompatible with such purpose. To disclose data only to authorised persons or organisations as instructed by Spencer Private Hospitals. Customer Care It is the aim of the hospital to provide patients and clients with the best possible care and service. In order to meet this aim all of our staff are required, at all times, to put the patient or client first and do their utmost to meet their requests and needs courteously and efficiently. Confidentiality To ensure that confidential information is not disclosed about Spencer Private Hospitals (including information regarding patients and staff) to any unauthorised member of staff, or to anyone outside the employment of Spencer Private Hospitals. This job description is intended to reflect, in outline, the responsibilities of the post holder, which may change over time with corporate or local business needs of Spencer Private Hospitals. It will therefore be subject to periodic review and amendment in the light of changing circumstances and following consultation with the post holder.

title: Receptionist- St Peters Surgery
description: Invicta Health is recruiting for a Receptionist to join the team on a part time basis at St Peters Surgery. Working hours per week: 18 hours Fixed term for 12 months We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. As an Administrative Receptionist, you will provide an important role in supporting the practice team with the day-to-day running of the practice by undertaking a variety of general and clinical administration duties. You will act as the first point of contact for patients contacting the practice, and work effectively to receive, assist, and direct them in accessing the appropriate healthcare professional or service in a courteous manner ensuring confidentiality. You will provide a welcoming, friendly, and positive image to patients and visitors either in person, via email or via the telephone, portraying the practice in the highest possible professional basis. Front Desk Tend to the front desk ensuring to greet patients and visitors on their arrival to the practice in a welcoming manner. Ensure all patients and visitors to the practice are signed in and directed to the relevant waiting area. Inform the relevant host for example, the GP, Nurse or Practice Manager of any patients or visitors arrival. Accept payments and issue receipts for non-NHS services. Book ambulances/appropriate transport for patients according to protocols. Assist patients with requests for Blood Forms, Urine Forms and Xray forms, printing where necessary. Keep the reception area, noticeboards, and leaflet dispensers clean, tidy and free from obstructions and clutter. Support in ensuring the reception area remains a calm environment for all. Politely and safely addressing any disruptive behaviours, escalating to management where appropriate. Registrations and Appointments Process registrations both regular and temporary in the absence of the Registration Clerk ensuring complete information and appropriate ID. Assess and analyse patient needs to ensure an appointment is required and if so, booked with the correct and appropriate healthcare professional. Book, amend and cancel general (GP/Nurse), clinic (Flu), QOF, special allocation services (SAS) and third party (Physio) patient appointments in line with practice appointment procedures, ensuring coding is completed where necessary and optimum efficiency of the appointment system. Monitor the incoming E-Consult messages booking an appropriate appointment or directing to the most appropriate department. Monitor the 111 clinical screen and directing as appropriate Ensure that patients without appointments but who need 'urgent consultations are booked into appropriate slots and referred to a GP where necessary. Receive and accurately record requests for home visits, assessing urgency in accordance with the Practices protocols. Once trained, chaperone patients to their GP appointment as and when requested. Arrange security for Special Allocation Service (SAS) appointments where necessary. Prescriptions and Certificates Receive and process prescription requests in the absence of the Prescription Clerk accurately and in accordance with practice guidelines Raise any prescription queries with the Prescription Clerk and/or Clinical Lead including status check of whether it has been issued and where it is. Processing and handling of Cremation Forms and Death Certificates, informing required departments and accurately documenting details of passing. Advice and guidance Provide advice (non-medical) and contact details of third-party services to patients as required. For example, suggesting a patient contact the Urgent Mental Health Team. Respond to and/or redirect all general enquiries, explaining procedures where necessary and processing paperwork where required. Process referrals for the District Nurse Action EMIS tasks and DOCMAN workflow in a timely manner Communication Answer incoming telephone calls in a timely and professional manner, ensuring calls are documented and actioned and/or redirected as appropriate. Communicate with GPs, Nurses, and the Clinical Team as necessary including passing information across to be processed, chasing documentation, results, and appointment information. Communicate in writing (letters and electronically) and verbally with a wide range of providers and users of services, including patients, carers; voluntary; social; primary and secondary care providers. Liaising with GP/Clinicians, forwarding concerns, chasing for samples, letters, prescriptions and other paperwork Monitor the reception email account and action any requests needed, raising any urgent enquiries to your line manager where relevant Process any outgoing mail created by the reception team Data Handling Document information received from patients or third-party agencies, accurately on EMIS. For example, urgent blood results from path labs, patients home blood pressure readings and any urgent referral advise provided to them. Undertake manual and electronic filing and retrieving of paperwork ensuring up-to-date maintenance of both computerised and manual filing systems (i.e. patient notes). Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures. Accessing the server, changing the tape and checking back up has been successful, reporting to IT if any issues are identified. Equipment and Stock Control Efficient filling of sample pots, testing kits, appointment cards, registration paperwork and other necessary aids. Clearing and re-stocking stationery items in work areas as required, ensuring low stock levels are reported to the relevant leads and ensuring a clear desk policy. Safely accept and record receipt of any vaccine/medication deliveries, ensuring safe storage of items and informing relevant departments. Miscellaneous Opening and locking up of practice premises (where needed) and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols at all times. Keep up to date with any new guidance and changes within the team. Supporting in the training of new reception team members. General Duties To work collaboratively and professionally with colleagues across Invicta Health, building and maintaining relationships. To contribute to the development of services, including processes, templates and principles. To take part in any statutory and mandatory training or other training and development programmes as requested. Any other reasonable duties as directed by your line manager.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Medical Receptionist / Administrator Sheppey Healthy Living Centre About the Role We are looking for a friendly, approachable and organised Medical Receptionist / Administrator to join our team at Sheppey Healthy Living Centre. The post is for 15 hours per week. Our reception team plays a vital role in supporting patients and ensuring the smooth running of our busy GP practice. As a receptionist, you will often be the first point of contact for patients, whether face-to-face, over the telephone or through electronic communications. This is a varied role that combines patient-facing reception duties with general administrative tasks. You will need to be able to work in a busy environment, communicate effectively with patients and colleagues, and approach your work with patience, professionalism and attention to detail. No previous experience is necessary, as full training will be provided. We are looking for someone with the right attitude, a willingness to learn and a commitment to providing excellent patient service. Key Responsibilities Welcoming patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and helpful manner. Answering incoming telephone calls and dealing with patient enquiries appropriately. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments in line with practice procedures. Managing patient information accurately and maintaining confidentiality at all times. Carrying out general administrative duties, including filing, scanning, emailing, processing documents and updating electronic records. Handling incoming and outgoing correspondence and allocating information to the appropriate members of the team. Supporting clinicians and colleagues with administrative tasks to help ensure the efficient running of the practice. Following practice policies and procedures, including those relating to confidentiality, data protection and patient safety. We are looking for a friendly, approachable and organised Medical Receptionist / Administrator to join our team at Minster Medical Group. What We Are Looking For We are interested in candidates who can demonstrate: A friendly, caring and professional approach to patients and colleagues. Good communication skills, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Basic IT skills and the confidence to learn new computer systems. Good organisational skills and attention to detail. The ability to remain calm, polite and professional when working under pressure. A flexible and reliable approach to work. The ability to work independently when required, while also being a supportive member of a team. A willingness to learn and follow practice procedures. Previous reception, administration or healthcare experience is not required. We welcome applications from candidates looking to develop new skills and begin a career in general practice. Working Hours The practice operates Monday to Friday, between 8:00 am and 6:30 pm. Flexibility is essential, as working hours will need to fit within the practice's operational requirements. Why Join Us? This is an opportunity to become part of a friendly and dedicated team, supporting the delivery of primary healthcare to our local community. Full training will be provided, and you will have the opportunity to develop your skills in both reception and medical administration. If you are approachable, reliable, willing to learn and enjoy helping people, we would love to hear from you. Join Minster Medical Group and make a difference to our patients and community. Working Environment and Team At Sheppey Healthy Living Centre, we believe that every member of our team is valued and plays an important part in providing a high-quality service to our patients. Regardless of role or level of responsibility, we encourage a supportive, inclusive and respectful working environment where everyone is treated as an equal and has the opportunity to contribute to the success of the practice. We recognise the importance of teamwork, communication and ongoing development. We provide training opportunities, hold regular team meetings and encourage staff to share ideas, learn new skills and support one another. We also value the importance of building positive working relationships outside the workplace, with team dinners, social evenings and other opportunities to get together. We want our staff to feel welcomed, supported and part of the wider team, not simply defined by their individual job role. Please note that our Sheppey Healthy Living Centre site is currently closed, and staff are therefore working from our Minster Medical Centre site. Current working arrangements are based at Minster Medical Centre until further notice. Job Description Practice Receptionist Job Summary As a Practice Receptionist at Sheppey Healthy Living Centre, you will play an important role in supporting patients and ensuring the smooth running of our busy GP practice. You will be one of the first points of contact for patients, providing a welcoming, professional and helpful service both face-to-face and over the telephone. The role involves a combination of reception duties and general administration. You will work closely with clinicians, administrative colleagues and the wider practice team to help ensure patients receive the appropriate care and support. No previous experience in general practice is required, as training will be provided. We are looking for someone who is reliable, organised, approachable and willing to learn. Main Duties and Responsibilities Reception and Patient Services Welcome patients and visitors, check patients in for appointments and provide assistance in a polite and professional manner. Answer telephone calls, respond to patient enquiries and direct queries to the appropriate team member. Book, amend and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Record patient contacts and information accurately on the clinical system. Handle requests for home visits, ensuring relevant information is recorded and passed to the appropriate clinician. Maintain effective communication between patients, clinicians and other members of the practice team. Receive payments for private services where applicable and issue receipts. Administrative Duties Carry out general administrative tasks, including scanning, photocopying, filing, emailing and processing correspondence. Manage electronic messages, patient tasks and documents through the practice's computer systems. Assist with patient registrations and ensure relevant paperwork is completed and passed to the appropriate team. Support the processing of investigation results, clinical correspondence and other patient-related information in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain information leaflets and other patient information, ensuring they are available and up to date. Undertake other administrative duties as required to support the effective running of the practice. Prescriptions and Patient Records Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice protocols and agreed timescales. Send prescriptions electronically where appropriate. Maintain accurate patient records and handle confidential information responsibly. Follow established procedures when processing prescription requests and other patient-related tasks. Teamwork and Communication Work collaboratively with reception colleagues, clinicians and the wider practice team. Communicate clearly and professionally with patients, carers, colleagues and external organisations. Follow practice policies, procedures and written protocols. Attend team meetings, complete mandatory training and participate in learning and development activities. Manage workload effectively and contribute to improving the quality and efficiency of practice services. Health, Safety and Security Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with data protection requirements at all times. Follow health and safety, infection prevention and control, safeguarding, equality and diversity policies. Report concerns, risks or potential hazards to the appropriate person. Follow building security procedures, including opening, closing and securing the premises when required. Undertake other reasonable duties as requested by the management team. Person Specification We welcome applications from candidates with a positive attitude who are keen to learn and develop new skills. The successful candidate will demonstrate: A friendly, helpful and professional approach to patients and colleagues. Good verbal and written communication skills. Good IT skills and a willingness to learn new computer systems. The ability to work effectively as part of a team and independently when required. The ability to remain calm, courteous and professional in a busy environment. Reliability, flexibility and a willingness to undertake training. An understanding of the importance of confidentiality, patient dignity and respectful communication. Previous reception, administration or healthcare experience is desirable but not essential. Full training will be provided. Working Arrangements The practice operates Monday to Friday, between 8:00 am and 6:30 pm. Flexibility is required to meet the operational needs of the practice, including participation in rota arrangements and occasional additional hours where agreed. The post-holder will report to the Operational Manager and will be expected to work in accordance with practice policies, procedures and relevant professional standards. The duties outlined above are not exhaustive and may be amended in consultation with the post-holder to meet the changing needs of the practice.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential. Job Description Clinical Administrator Job Title: Clinical Administrator Responsible to: Administration Lead, Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Partnership Hours: Applicants must be available to work within our core operating hours of 08:00-17:30 . We are open to discussing flexibility around shift length and working patterns for the right candidate. Job Summary The Clinical Administrator provides vital support to the multidisciplinary team by managing and processing clinical correspondence and patient records in line with practice and national guidelines. The role focuses on streamlining workflows to reduce unnecessary GP administration, ensuring accurate coding and filing of information, and directing more complex items to the appropriate clinician for review. The post-holder will work as part of the Clinical Administration team, prioritising their workload effectively, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times, and knowing when to escalate matters to supervisors or clinicians. Roles and Responsibilities Ensure all incoming and internal correspondence is stored in patient records. Review and Read Code clinical correspondence before forwarding to clinicians. Process and file hospital letters, reports, emails and other correspondence. Code diagnoses, procedures and investigations accurately. Refer complex or high-risk documents, including safeguarding issues, to the relevant clinician. Summarise new patient records (manual and GP2GP) and process registrations, transfers, and out-of-area notifications. Manage incoming test results, redirect unmatched pathology, and process screening and monitoring results. Process Out of Hours reports and other external communications. Monitor the practice email inbox, flagging urgent queries promptly. Provide administrative cover for other team members when necessary. Open, scan, distribute and file post; manage photocopying and record requests. Assist with training and mentoring of new staff. Maintain a tidy office environment and adhere to a clear desk policy. Teamwork & Communication Work as part of the Clinical Administration Team and the wider practice team. Build effective working relationships with colleagues, patients and external organisations. Communicate clearly and professionally, ensuring confidentiality at all times. Participate in meetings and training, including occasional sessions outside normal hours. General Responsibilities Confidentiality Patients entrust the practice with sensitive information and staff must respect this confidentiality at all times. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues or the practice may only be shared in line with GDPR and practice policies. Health & Safety Follow practice health and safety policies, including infection prevention and control. Use personal security systems as required. Identify risks, manage work safely, and report concerns promptly. Maintain work areas in a safe, hazard-free condition. Equality & Diversity Promote equality of opportunity and respect the rights of patients, carers and colleagues. Act in ways that recognise diversity and ensure fairness, consistent with policy and legislation. Respect privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs at all times. Personal & Professional Development Participate in annual appraisal and performance reviews. Take responsibility for ongoing learning and development. Share skills and knowledge with colleagues and support new staff training. Quality Strive to maintain quality and safety within the practice. Reflect on individual and team activities, suggesting improvements to enhance performance. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Communication Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external agencies. Adapt communication methods to meet individual needs and ensure understanding. Other Information Duties may change according to practice needs, following consultation and training. The role is subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act (1974) exceptions, requiring disclosure of relevant convictions. The practice operates a non-smoking policy.
